findings.title: "Read-side over 300's write path" rests on a persisted record that cannot be keyed, joined, or trended
findings.description:
The principle says 320 "reads and annotates that record; it does not modify the judging path… or the result models' write semantics", and Non-Goals repeats "No change to the judging path." The keystone slice needs human verdicts "keyed to persisted judge results (with judge-configuration identity)". What 300 actually persists (`src/squadron/review/persistence.py`) does not allow this:

- **No result identity.** A result is a file named `{index}-review.{review_type}.{slice_name}.md` (`save_review_file`, `save_review_result`). There is no run ID or result ID to attach a sample to.
- **No history.** `path.write_text` overwrites the same filename on every re-review. In a 303 review→fix→re-review cycle, only the last judgment survives. A human verdict attached to iteration 1 becomes silently attached to iteration 3's score, and the "trend over time" in Envisioned State has no data.
- **Multi-sample runs collide.** N judges or N runs on the same artifact write the same filename unless a `name_suffix` is threaded through. Opportunistic dispersion capture ("when multi-sample ran anyway") has nothing to read; the median reduction discards the samples.
- **Incomplete judge-configuration identity.** The markdown frontmatter emits `reviewType` and `aiModel` (which falls back to the literal `"unknown"`), but not `template_name`, and no template version or content hash exists anywhere. The code comment says provenance is "never emitted here".
- **"Queryable" means frontmatter.** The score is a YAML frontmatter line in a per-project markdown file, not a column or index. Any aggregate query is a directory scan plus a parse of every file.

Meeting the document's own "keyed by judge configuration is fixed here" commitment requires write-path changes: a stable result ID, append-not-overwrite, template identity/version, and retained per-sample results. The document must either drop the read-only principle and Non-Goal and name the write-path additions as the first slice, or show how identity and history are obtained without them. As written, the keystone slice will discover this mid-design.

findings.title: Metrology store, the keystone decision, is deferred while everything depends on it
findings.description:
"Where metrology data lives" names cross-project aggregation as "a new requirement" and then defers the choice (extend existing storage, add a new store, or use 280) to slice design. This is the architectural decision, not a slice detail:

- **Join across unlike stores.** Judge results are markdown files inside each project's repo. A cross-project store must reference them by a key that survives repo moves, branch switches, worktrees and file overwrites. No such key is defined (see the FAIL above).
- **280 is not a real option.** It is `not_started`, and the initiative plan declares 320 "Independent of… 280". Listing it as a candidate leaves a dependency ambiguity open.
- **Ownership is unstated.** The document does not say whether human samples are committed to the project repo (in-repo, versioned, per-project) or kept in a user-level store (cross-project, unversioned). Each gives different answers for multi-worktree use and for whether calibration travels with the project.

Commit to one here. The lightest option consistent with the stack is in-repo sample records beside the review files, plus a user-level aggregation command that scans registered projects.

findings.title: Tech-debt-audit harness has no execution path in squadron
findings.description:
"Run the audit across squadron-managed projects, normalize and persist findings" assumes squadron can invoke the audit. Per 340, the audit is a Claude Code slash-command markdown file copied to `~/.claude/commands/analysis/`, invoked interactively as `/sq:analysis tech-debt`. The document leaves four things unspecified:

- **How it runs headlessly.** Candidates are a `dispatch` step with the skill body as prompt, an SDK session, or a new action. The audit is multi-step, tool-using and file-reading, which 300 forbids inside judges; whether a dispatch-based run is acceptable here is not stated.
- **What "squadron-managed projects" means.** I found no project registry in the document or in the references I checked. The cross-project enumeration source is undefined.
- **Normalization.** "Normalizing an LLM-authored audit" to (category, location, severity) is the hard part, and it is given one sentence. The skill's output format is owned by a forked external skill. Either the skill is modified to emit a structured block (a 340-pack change, not mentioned) or a second LLM pass extracts it, which adds its own variance. Project parsing rules require fixtures from the real output format, so the format must be pinned.
- **Skill naming.** 340-arch calls it `tech-debt-analyze`; 340-slices and this document call it `tech-debt-audit`. Confirm which file actually ships.

findings.title: Pre-emption delta is unlikely to be detectable with the stated design
findings.description:
Design Goals claim the pre-emption slice proves "the metrology can detect an intervention's effect". The document's own caveats undercut this:

- The audit is "non-deterministic run-to-run" and the baseline is "a handful of projects".
- The comparison is an observational before/after, with no control group.
- No step measures the audit's own run-to-run variance (repeat audits on an unchanged commit) before the delta is interpreted. Without that noise floor, any drop is uninterpretable.
- The unit is wrong. "Audit-findings-per-project" on an existing codebase is dominated by pre-existing code. The prompt only affects newly dispatched code, so the measure must be scoped to code written after the intervention (per slice or per diff).
- There is circularity: the prompt is authored from the audit's finding classes and then graded by the same audit. A drop may show the model learned to avoid the oracle's triggers, not that the code improved.

Add an audit repeatability measurement as a precondition of the baseline slice and redefine the delta unit.

findings.title: Sampling policy and metrics deferred, though they determine whether the output is valid
findings.description:
The document says "a biased sample yields a biased agreement number" and still leaves the selection policy to slice design. Three gaps follow:

- **Opportunistic sampling is biased by construction.** The human naturally sees escalated results, meaning judge FAIL/CONCERNS. Auto-passed results are never looked at, yet the false-pass rate is the quantity that matters for loosening a gate. The architecture must require that some auto-passed results are offered for sampling; otherwise the feedback slice recommends on exactly the wrong evidence.
- **The human verdict is undefined.** It could be PASS/CONCERNS/FAIL, agree/disagree with the judge, or a 0–100 score. Agree/disagree is anchored on having seen the judge's output; blind scoring is not "seconds". This choice fixes the record schema of the keystone slice.
- **The evidence floor may be unreachable.** Records are split by artifact level × template version × model, with "a handful" of samples per level, and any template or model change invalidates the cell. For a solo operator the floor may never be met, leaving the feedback slice permanently inert. State an expected sample volume and a pooling/compatibility rule, or accept that the feedback slice is a documentation deliverable.

findings.title: Dispersion measurement depends on unbuilt 300 future work
findings.description: "The execution machinery exists — 300's multi-sample option and 140's `fan_out`" is not accurate. Multi-Sample Judging is unchecked Future Work item 1 in `300-slices` (`[ ]`, effort 2/5). It is also specified as N runs reduced by median, which discards the dispersion 320 wants. And it is same-judge repetition; the "X overreaches, Y rubber-stamps" question needs different models on the same artifact, which is a different fan-out. The initiative plan says 320 itself runs multiple judges through the provider registry. The document should own a dedicated calibration-run mechanism that retains per-sample results, as an explicit slice or part of one, and stop pointing at 300.

findings.title: Frontmatter omits the 340 dependency
findings.description: `dependencies: [100, 140, 300]`, yet two of five slices cannot exist without the 340 analysis pack, and Related Work and 340-arch both name 320 as its primary consumer. The initiative plan has the same omission. Add 340, or split the code-quality half out (next finding).

findings.title: Two loosely related initiatives bundled; the shared "metrology shape" is thin
findings.description:
"Two oracles… one metrology shape, so the reporting layer is built once" does not hold up against the data:

| | Judge calibration | Code-quality baseline |
|---|---|---|
| Record | Paired categorical/numeric judgments on one artifact | Counts of normalized findings per project |
| Statistic | Agreement and dispersion | Before/after count delta |
| Depends on | 300 | 340 |
| Customer | 300's threshold config | Dispatch prompts |

A reporting layer built to cover both is a premature abstraction over two schemas that share only "has a timestamp and an n". The plan assigns both to 320, so keep both, but:

- Cut the claim of a shared reporting layer and design each half's records and reports independently.
- Order the judge-calibration slices first; they are the stated reason 320 exists.
- Do not build "trend over time" in the first reporting slice; at a handful of samples it is noise.
- Scope the calibration-to-threshold slice honestly. Non-Goals forbid auto-mutation, so it is a report column ("meets floor: yes/no") plus documentation, not a mechanism.

findings.title: Capture surface, the stated make-or-break problem, has no design
findings.description:
"Sampling capture ergonomics… is the make-or-break design problem" is followed only by constraints (CLI, seconds, unambiguous attachment). Not addressed:

- **Where the operator is.** In an unattended 303 cycle the operator is absent at judgment time; they are present only at checkpoint escalation, which is the biased slice above. No interaction is described for sampling auto-passed results after the fact (a `sq` subcommand listing unsampled results? a prompt at pipeline end?).
- **Staleness.** By capture time the artifact may have been fixed and re-judged. Without a snapshot or commit SHA on the judge result, the human is judging a different artifact than the judge did.
- **Surface parity.** "Honoring interface parity if other surfaces are added" is undefined against squadron's actual surfaces (the `sq` CLI and `/sq:*` slash commands).

findings.title: Artifact level is not a recorded field
findings.description: "Calibration is per artifact level" requires every judge result to carry its level. The persisted record has only `reviewType` (a free label) and, in JSON output, the template name such as `judge.slice-vs-arch`. Deriving the level from a template name uses a user-accessible label as logical structure, which project rules forbid. Define an explicit artifact-level enum on the judge template and result.

findings.title: `criteria` map mentioned with no use
findings.description: "Where a latent field exists (e.g. the reserved `criteria` map), 320 populates or reads it" — no goal, slice or report uses per-criterion scores. Populating it would require changing judge templates, which contradicts "does not modify the judging path". Remove the sentence, or state the use.

structured_findings.summary: "Read-side over 300's write path" rests on a persisted record that cannot be keyed, joined, or trended
Metrology store, the keystone decision, is deferred while everything depends on it
Tech-debt-audit harness has no execution path in squadron
Pre-emption delta is unlikely to be detectable with the stated design
Sampling policy and metrics deferred, though they determine whether the output is valid
Dispersion measurement depends on unbuilt 300 future work
Two loosely related initiatives bundled; the shared "metrology shape" is thin
Capture surface, the stated make-or-break problem, has no design
Artifact level is not a recorded field
